Root Cause: After an OS patch swap-rebalance, decommissioned nodes were not drained from the AWS Network Load Balancer target group for port 18093 (N1QL). The NLB continued routing ~⅓ of queries to the stale, unhealthy nodes — causing connection resets and timeouts for all services connecting via the NLB endpoint.

Resolution: Couchbase Capella engineering applied a backend fix on Jun 29 to flush the stale NLB target group entries. WU confirmed N1QL connectivity restored. Ticket remains open pending CB documentation of the fix procedure — WU requires this before their next OS upgrade cycle can proceed.

CB engineers maintained sub-hour response gaps throughout the critical period (Jun 25–26). ESC-3538 raised to engage Capella engineering directly. Fix deployed Jun 29, 4 days after open.

#78964 Query Timeout — UnambiguousTimeoutException (Workflow_Manager)
P4 Analysis Delivered
Opened Jun 19 Assignee Ramya Bhaskar Area Server · Data Service Last update Jun 29
Cluster — iWatchX / Workflow_Manager
f7885917-505d…
Production
CB Version7.6.3-4211
Nodes9 (3D / 3Q / 3I)
RAM / CPU32 GB · 8 vCPU/node
Indexes346 GSI

Event window: Jun 19, 4:35–5:05 PM ET. Observed 900–1000 disk read IOPS spike, elevated write IOPS and write queue depth.

Root Cause (Ramya's analysis, Jun 29): A query scanning 1.25 million index entries then fetching 1.25 million full documents (696 MB RAM) to return only 40 results hit the 75-second query timeout. This coincided with heavy concurrent compaction across large buckets plus XDCR pipeline connection errors adding background strain.

Recommendation: The query is severely unoptimized — index selection is working but the fetch phase is doing full-document retrieval where a covering index would eliminate it. Ramya has referred this to Professional Services for query and index design review, and notified AM AE_NAME to coordinate engagement.

ℹ
WU to confirm: Are timeouts still occurring? Is this a new pattern starting Jun 18 or recurring? Ramya is awaiting confirmation before determining whether to close.
#78970 Proactive: Scheduled Backup Failed — bucket CustomerProfile
P4 Resolved Archive Imminent

Cluster
Pharos-UAT
UAT
CB Version7.6.3
BucketCustomerProfile
Bucket Quota200 MB/node
ErrorETMPFAIL (vBucket 877)

Root Cause: Transient ETMPFAIL (temporary vBucket failure) on the backup DCP stream — a known intermittent issue in CB 7.6.3. CB 7.6.6 includes a retry improvement (MB-64077) that handles this automatically.

Resolution: Pavvan triggered a manual backup retry which completed successfully (Jun 21). Recommendations issued: increase CustomerProfile memory quota above 200 MB/node; plan upgrade path to CB 7.6.6 to prevent recurrence. No response from WU since Jun 21 — ticket auto-archives today.
